name: Amantadine
drug_class: Adamantane; NMDA receptor antagonist and former influenza A M2 ion channel inhibitor
route_note: Oral capsules, tablets and syrup; extended-release forms taken at bedtime or in the morning.
originator: E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company

discovery.note: Antiviral activity against influenza A was reported in 1964; anti-parkinsonian effect was noticed by chance in 1969.

tagline: Old flu antiviral repurposed for Parkinson's disease and levodopa-induced dyskinesia
summary: Amantadine was introduced in the 1960s as an influenza A antiviral and was serendipitously found to relieve Parkinson's disease symptoms. Viral resistance has ended its antiviral role, but it remains the main oral drug for levodopa-induced dyskinesia.
mechanism: In Parkinson's disease amantadine acts mainly as a weak uncompetitive NMDA glutamate receptor antagonist, dampening overactive corticostriatal glutamate signalling that contributes to dyskinesia. It may also increase dopamine release and reduce reuptake.
Its antiviral effect came from blocking the M2 proton channel of influenza A, preventing viral uncoating; a single S31N mutation now present in almost all circulating strains confers resistance.
uses: Parkinson's disease and drug-induced extrapyramidal reactions
Influenza A prophylaxis and treatment (historical; no longer recommended because of resistance)

history.title: Antiviral activity
history.detail: DuPont scientists report activity of amantadine against influenza A viruses.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Symmetrel is approved for prophylaxis of Asian (A2) influenza.

history.title: Parkinson's discovery
history.detail: Robert Schwab reports improvement of parkinsonism after a patient taking amantadine for influenza noticed her tremor eased.

history.title: Influenza recommendation withdrawn
history.detail: The US CDC advises against adamantanes for influenza because of widespread resistance.

history.title: Gocovri
history.detail: The FDA approves extended-release amantadine (Gocovri) for dyskinesia in Parkinson's disease.

history.title: Osmolex ER
history.detail: A second extended-release amantadine tablet is approved for Parkinson's disease and drug-induced extrapyramidal reactions.

pk.half_life: about 10–17 hours, longer in older people and renal impairment

serious: Neuroleptic malignant-like syndrome on abrupt withdrawal

facts: The chance observation of amantadine's anti-parkinsonian effect came from a patient taking it for influenza prophylaxis.
